title: On the Structure of Risk Contribution: A Leave-One-Out Decomposition into Inherent and Correlation Risk
summary: This paper proposes a methodological decomposition of portfolio Risk Contribution (RC) into two components: inherent risk (independent of portfolio correlations) and correlation risk (driven by covariance with other holdings). The framework uses a leave-one-out approach that preserves strict additivity and applies to standard RC calculations. Two time-series approaches are presented for tracking how these components evolve across market regimes.
key_points: Decomposes standard Risk Contribution into inherent risk (always positive, reflecting standalone volatility) and correlation risk (may be positive or negative depending on covariance structure)
Uses a leave-one-out representation where each position's RC separates into a standalone volatility term and a covariance term with the remainder of the portfolio
The decomposition preserves strict additivity property of standard RC
Enables distinction between positions that contribute risk due to high standalone volatility versus high correlation with the portfolio
Provides diagnostic insight for identifying negatively correlated positions serving as effective hedges
Two time-series approaches proposed for tracking inherent vs. correlation risk across market regimes
why_it_matters: This methodological paper provides portfolio risk managers with a more granular diagnostic tool for understanding risk contributions. By separating inherent from correlation risk, practitioners can better attribute portfolio risk sources and assess whether risk changes during stress periods stem from volatility shifts, correlation changes, or both. The paper claims the approach is stable, transparent, and implementable for reporting, stress testing, and performance attribution.
